newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ford German unit to report loss - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Ford German unit to report loss - magazine.

text.p: Ford Werke AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker Ford Motor Co, will report a loss of at least 500 million marks ($295 million) for 1996, a German magazine said in a report on Monday.
Germany's "Capital" magazine said losses at the troubled unit of Ford could rise to almost as high as 600 million marks.
Ford's German unit reported a 1995 profit of 271 million marks in 1995. Ford will release its 1996 results at a news conference on March 25.

The losses were tied to start-up costs for Ford's new small vehicles -- the Ka and the Puma -- and also for overly-expensive parts contracts. The magazine also attributed some of the losses to recall actions by Ford.
A Ford spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
The magazine said the losses came at a time when Ford's 1996 sales rose by 21,000 vehicles to almost 400,000 vehicles and the carmaker's German market share rose to 11 percent.
